results.title: Playback FAQs
results.summary: The help center's Playback FAQ article has two questions. (1) How do I get song content for Playback: five documented ways: Playback Rentals (recommended, cheapest for weekly use), purchasing Artist Original Master Track products on MultiTracks.com (buy once, stays available for your location; extra licenses for additional campuses), uploading your own content with Cloud Pro (multitracks or single-file backing tracks, then add click, guide and song sections), using just the Click & Guide for any catalog song (requires Cloud Pro, Live Bundle, or Playback Rentals), and Sounds content (ambient pads and Soundbeds purchased on MultiTracks.com appear in Playback for free). (2) Does Playback show lyrics or chords: No. Playback is audio-first and does not display lyrics or charts.

steps.text: To get songs: unlock a Playback Rental, buy the track product on MultiTracks.com, upload your own content with Cloud Pro, use Click & Guide only (Cloud Pro, Live Bundle, or Rentals), or use purchased Sounds pads and Soundbeds.
Playback does not display lyrics or chord charts; it is audio-first. (ChartBuilder is MultiTracks' charts product; charts are out of Playback support scope.)

results.title: Playback Subscriptions | Explained
results.summary: Separates Playback Features (Intro, Premium, Cloud Pro, Live Bundle), Playback Content (Rentals, purchased tracks, Sounds, uploaded Cloud Songs, click and guide), and Playback Access (Team Sharing seats). Playback Intro is free on iOS, iPadOS, and macOS but limited to a single stereo output and excludes Premium features (editing arrangements, Playback Remote, Playback Sync). Cloud Pro adds click and guide for every song, Team Sharing seats, and saved custom-named arrangements; uploading Cloud Songs requires Cloud Pro. Rentals are device-specific and not shared. The article does not explain how to check or manage the subscription in-app.

results.title: Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues
results.summary: Focuses on dropouts and disconnections in live setups. Four checks: device/OS/app up to date, iOS performance (RAM, background apps), the USB connection (named as the most common cause in MultiOut setups), and the audio connection (Auto Pan splitter cable, class-compliant interfaces). The article does not cover no-sound, output selection, Bluetooth, sample rate, or mono/stereo settings.

steps.text: Check the device is supported (supported devices list for iOS, iPadOS, macOS). On the oldest supported iOS generation, Multi-Outs and MIDI Cue editing are limited.
Confirm the OS is up to date and that Playback support for it is confirmed (see the OS compatibility article). Update Playback from the iOS or Mac App Store.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: iOS performance: clear RAM, force-close all background apps before opening Playback, and do not multitask during a live performance.
USB adapter: an official Apple adapter is required (Lightning to USB3 or USB-C to USB3; both allow simultaneous charging).
USB cable length: max 16 feet for USB 2.0, 3 meters (9 feet) for USB 3.0. Keep the digital USB run short and use longer analog runs (XLR, 1/4") from the interface to DI boxes and the console.
Powered USB extension cables: base cable must respect the limits above; the active repeater needs external power; max extender length 25 m (USB 2.0) or 15 m (USB 3.0).
Powered USB hub: must be powered, no more than 7 USB accessory ports, and only one audio interface connected at a time so Playback sends audio to the correct device.
Auto Pan splitter cable: use a high-quality cable with as few adaptors as possible.
Audio interface: Playback is generally compatible with class-compliant USB interfaces; check the tested supported devices list on multitracks.com.
If issues persist, contact MultiTracks support.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > App Overview > Login Requirements > Organizations vs. Users
results.text: An organization in the MultiTracks.com ecosystem is the umbrella under which content can be purchased, users can be added, and subscriptions can be shared. When an 'account' is created using the "Sign Up" flow, an organization and a user is created simultaneously and the user is set as the owner of the organization. When logging into Playback, there is an organization selection prompt, to select which organization to log into. If you are a user belonging only to the organization created when you built your account, then select that organization. However, a user can be added to other existing MultiTracks.com organizations and have access to content belonging to those organizations in Playback. Every organization that you've been added to will be available at this login screen.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Building a Setlist > The Setlists Menu > How to Use Setlists | Video Guide
results.text: Setlists created from MultiTracks.com, ChartBuilder, or another Playback device in an organization can be opened directly in Playback. As previously mentioned, content and user permissions apply when opening a setlist with purchased or rented tracks. To ensure setlist synchronization and accessibility, always save setlists to the cloud. This ensures they can be accessed across multiple devices linked to your MultiTracks.com account.

results.title: Playback product page FAQ (multitracks.com)
results.summary: Five FAQs on the Playback product page. How do I add a song: tap 'Add a Song' and select a song; after the first, keep adding in edit mode with the '+' button. Can I upload my own content: yes, with a Cloud Pro subscription (also included in the Live Bundle or MultiTracks One); create a cloud song, upload stems/audio files, and they appear in Playback. How many devices: log in on up to 2 devices; a Premium subscription adds a 3rd device slot; devices are managed in your MultiTracks.com account. Can I give my team access: yes, add a person to your account and enable Playback Team Sharing to share your purchased library and MultiTracks Cloud content. Can I use an audio interface: yes, see the tested supported-devices list. The page also says Playback for Mac supports Dante with up to 32 outputs and that Premium includes up to 32 MultiOuts with buses and redundancy with PlayAudio 12.

steps.text: Add a song: tap 'Add a Song' in Playback and select a song. After the first song, add more in edit mode with the '+' button.
Upload your own content: requires Cloud Pro (included in Live Bundle or MultiTracks One). Create a cloud song, upload your stems or audio files, and they appear in Playback.
Device limit: Playback can be logged in on up to 2 devices; Premium adds a 3rd slot. Manage devices in your MultiTracks.com account (see 'Managing ChartBuilder and Playback Devices').
Team access: add the person to your account and enable Playback Team Sharing so they can use your purchased library and Cloud content.
Audio interfaces: supported, see the tested list at https://www.multitracks.com/products/playback/supported.

results.title: Playback User Guide
results.summary: The master user guide. Relevant documented points: the Audio Device setting (Settings > General > Audio Device) chooses the device Playback uses for all audio output; Auto Pan sends click/guide left and tracks right on the headphone output; MultiOuts (Premium) allow up to 32 outputs; track routing lives in Settings > Tracks and bus routing in Settings > Buses; purchased tracks download free; downloaded setlists stay on the device until removed or until a different user signs in; Settings > About has Manage Subscription and Restore Purchases.

steps.text: Select the output device: tap the stack icon (top-right) > Settings > General > Audio Device.

Auto Pan: Settings > General > Auto-Pan. Sends click and guide to the left output and all tracks to the right output of the device's stereo output, so you can run tracks from the headphone port without an interface.
Track routing: Settings > Tracks, tap an instrument part and choose a bus. Routing is device-specific and applies to that track across all songs and setlists on that device.
Bus routing: Settings > Buses, tap a bus cell, choose an output, tap Done. Swipe left on a bus to edit its name/abbreviation. Bus routing is saved per audio device.
If an output is greyed out it may be in use by SMPTE: change the SMPTE routing or disable SMPTE output in General settings.

Download a song: when adding a song, tap Add in the top-right corner. In the Setlists menu, tap Open Setlist, select a setlist, and tap the download icons to download tracks without loading the setlist, or load it to download every song automatically. Songs already on the device from another setlist show no download icon.

Remove one setlist from the device: open it in the Setlists menu and choose Remove Setlist From Device. Remove all: Setlists menu > Delete All Setlists From Device. This does not delete setlists from your MultiTracks.com account; re-download from the setlist menu to recover.
steps.caution: This removes the song from the device and re-downloads it, so only do it when you have time before you play.

steps.text: Subscription not recognized: Settings > About > Restore Purchases. The guide says: if an iTunes subscription is expired or not being confirmed by Playback, reconcile any payment issues in the App Store and tap Restore Purchases to reconnect your In-App Subscription.
steps.caution: Updating the app closes Playback and takes a few minutes; don't do this during a service.

steps.text: Side menu (stack icon) shows user name, organization name and ID, Switch Organizations, and Log Out.
steps.caution: Signing out can interrupt cloud access until you sign back in.

results.title: How do I connect my USB audio interface to Playback?
results.summary: iOS-focused guide for connecting a USB audio interface, directly via an official Apple adapter or through a powered USB hub (required when also using a MIDI controller or Ethernet MIDI). Playback recognizes the interface as its audio device once connected. The article states Playback sends up to 10 individual outputs with instrument tracks routed to 10 buses; note that other articles (Track & Bus Routing, Sound System) cite 16 buses and up to 32 outputs, so this figure may be dated.

steps.text: Direct: connect the iOS device to an approved interface with an official Apple adapter (Lightning: Apple USB 3 to Lightning camera adapter; USB-C: Apple USB-C AV adapter). These allow charging while connected.

Via powered hub: connect the hub to the device with the Apple adapter, then connect the interface to the hub. Playback recognizes the interface as its audio device. Hubs the article confirms: 7-port Anker (1 charge port), 7-port Plugable (2 charge ports), 7-port StarTech.
Keep USB runs short: 16 ft max (USB 2.0), 3 m / 9 ft max (USB 3.0). Powered extenders: repeater needs external power; 25 m (USB 2.0) / 15 m (USB 3.0) max.
Hub must be powered and have no more than 7 accessory ports.
Further problems: see Troubleshooting Playback Audio Issues.

results.sectionPath: Playback User Guide > Playback Settings > Side Menu: Settings & Features
results.text:
Playback's side menu has the following features:

- Main Settings Menu
- Waveform Size: adjustment
- Notifications: To toggle in-app notifications on or off.
- Playback Sync: To enable or disable Playback Sync broadcast from the Playback device.
- Playback Remote: The main Playback Remote menu to initiate a Playback Remote session, and/or connect a remote Playback device to a host Playback device. (📖Learn More)
- Network: the area to select which specific IP Address or network Playback Sync and Playback Remote broadcast through on host devices. (When utilizing multiple IP addresses or networks on a MacOS device).
- User Name, Organization Name, and Organization ID Number.
- Switch Organizations to switch between available organizations the signed-in user has access to.
- Log Out to log out the currently signed-in user of Playback.

Opening "Settings" in Playback's side menu will reveal the main Settings menu with the five settings' tabs; General, Tacks, Buses, MIDI, and About.
